brief.prompt: Hard questions only for experts, 2 rounds of 10 on quantum physics

before.text: Which physicist introduced the quantum of action in 1900 while deriving the law of black-body radiation?
The 1927 experiment by Davisson and Germer confirmed the wave nature of electrons by diffracting them off a crystal of which metal?
In 1922, what property of silver atoms did the Stern–Gerlach experiment show to be quantised?
Which physicist proposed matter waves in his 1924 doctoral thesis?
What name is given to the 1935 paper by Einstein, Podolsky and Rosen, and to the paradox it describes, by its authors' initials?
Who formulated the exclusion principle in 1925?
Which physicist, working on Heligoland in 1925, made the breakthrough that led to matrix mechanics?
Which relativistic wave equation for the electron, published in 1928, predicted antimatter?
Whose 1964 theorem gave an inequality that any local hidden-variable theory must satisfy?
Who proposed the relative-state (many-worlds) interpretation in his 1957 thesis?
What is the name of the matrices σx, σy and σz used to describe spin one-half?
Which quantum effect predicts an attractive force between two uncharged parallel conducting plates in a vacuum?
Which effect, predicted in 1959, shows that an electron can be affected by electromagnetic potentials in a region where the fields are zero?
What is the maximum value of the CHSH combination of correlations allowed by quantum mechanics, known as Tsirelson's bound?
Which theorem states that an arbitrary unknown quantum state cannot be copied exactly?
The half-integer spin of fermions means their wavefunction changes sign under a rotation of how many degrees?
Which quantum algorithm, published in 1996, searches an unstructured database in about the square root of N steps?
Which theorem, proved by Kochen and Specker's contemporaries and named after them, rules out non-contextual hidden variables in Hilbert spaces of dimension three or more?
In quantum electrodynamics, what is the name of the small energy difference between the 2S½ and 2P½ levels of hydrogen, measured in 1947?
Which 1970 Nobel-winning... no—which state of matter, first made in a dilute gas of rubidium atoms in 1995, won Cornell, Wieman and Ketterle the 2001 Nobel Prize?

verdicts.reason: Checker's answer is the same thing put another way: spatial orientation of angular momentum.
False premise: Kochen and Specker proved the theorem themselves.
verdicts.text: Which theorem, proved in 1967 and named after the two mathematicians who proved it, rules out non-contextual hidden variables in Hilbert spaces of dimension three or more?

verdicts.reason: Garbled false start removed; Ketterle used sodium, so the rubidium claim now covers only the first condensate.
verdicts.text: Which state of matter, first made in a dilute gas of rubidium atoms in 1995, won Cornell, Wieman and Ketterle the 2001 Nobel Prize in Physics?

R1Q3.answer: The spatial orientation of their angular momentum (magnetic moment), i.e. spin
